scenario: An office manager wants to refill a shared candy drawer and is tempted to buy the highest-rated familiar chocolate listings. Four frozen seller pages show a Kinder Bueno five-pack at 9.99 dollars rated 98 percent over eight reviews, a personalized twelve-bar Hershey milk-chocolate pack at 22.00 dollars rated 100 percent over two reviews, a Godiva-branded six-carton mini-bar variety set packed by Candy Cabin at 36.95 dollars rated 100 percent over one review, and a two-pound Goldenberg dark-chocolate peanut-chew assortment repackaged by Emporium Candy at 14.99 dollars rated 95 percent over twelve reviews. The Goldenberg page repeats a seller claim that the product has the same quality and taste always known, but none of the four pages provides a dated historical ingredient panel or a matched old-versus-new package record. General corpus pages distinguish chocolate types, compound chocolate, couverture, jurisdiction-specific naming and fat rules, food-label fields, and comparable-unit pricing. Three community discussions contain anecdotes about reported quality decline after manufacturing changes, personal disagreement with high ratings in another domain, and snack-temperature effects. The corpus does not provide current physical package photographs, full current ingredient panels for all four exact offers, manufacturer-confirmed recipe histories, historical package weights and prices, dated matched SKU pairs, purchase receipts, office allergy and dietary requirements, or a controlled office taste and consumption trial.

rules.exact_offer_rating_sample_matrix_v1: The four frozen seller pages establish current page assertions, not independent quality histories. Kinder Bueno SKU B08ZHJY8NY is 9.99 dollars, rated 98 percent over eight reviews, and described as five 1.5-ounce packs with two individually wrapped bars per pack. Hershey SKU B084Q44G26 is 22.00 dollars, rated 100 percent over two reviews, and described as twelve individually wrapped 1.55-ounce personalized milk-chocolate bars with Hershey's in the manufacturer field. The Godiva-branded Candy Cabin page for SKU B08SFJWJK2 is 36.95 dollars, rated 100 percent over one review, and describes six cartons with eight mini bars each across roasted-almond dark, 72-percent cacao dark, and salted-caramel milk flavors, while its 3.1-ounce wording and Candy Cabin manufacturer field require exact package verification. Goldenberg SKU B07YST76HH is 14.99 dollars, rated 95 percent over twelve reviews, and described as two pounds of mini peanut chews repackaged in a broad-allergen facility by Emporium Candy. A displayed percentage must always travel with its review count, and none of these aggregates proves office preference, recipe stability, freshness, manufacturer identity beyond the page field, or delivered value.
rules.chocolate_label_and_fat_substitution_bou: The types page describes compound chocolate as cocoa combined with other vegetable fats in place of cocoa butter and presents different naming and fat rules for Canada and the EU. The couverture page says couverture has a higher cocoa-butter share, is legally regulated in the EU, is not a regulated term in the US, and is distinct from compound chocolate. The labeling page says food labeling is regulated in most jurisdictions and lists product identity, manufacturer and net quantity among US packaging fields. These general pages support a jurisdiction-and-label checklist; they do not classify any exact captured offer, prove its current fat source, establish that a recipe changed, or replace current primary rules and a physical ingredient label for the applicable market.
rules.recipe_weight_change_pairing_requirement: A formula-change, quality-downgrade, shrinkflation or skimpflation conclusion requires a dated before-and-after pair for the same SKU or a documented version mapping in the same market. For recipe claims, compare complete ingredient lists, fat source, order, declared formulation and manufacturer statements. For size and price claims, compare net quantity, pack count, total paid and price per common unit while preserving product form. The unit-price page explains comparable units across sizes and configurations. A current seller page, a nostalgic phrase, a rating, a product title, a packaging dimension, or an unrelated quality-decline anecdote cannot establish historical change.
rules.scoped_rating_reputation_temperature_tra: The BuyItForLife author reports non-chocolate examples of products allegedly declining after ownership or manufacturing changes; the books author reports personally rating popular high-average works much lower; and the snack thread reports a preference change after chilling chips. These sources motivate checks for dated version identity, individual-versus-aggregate disagreement and serving-temperature control. They are category-, author-, product- and condition-scoped anecdotes, not evidence that Kinder, Hershey, Godiva or Goldenberg changed recipe, shrank, deserves or does not deserve its displayed rating, or will win in this office.
rules.current_and_historical_verification_gate: Before judging an exact offer, obtain the current physical product name, seller, manufacturer or repacker, SKU or UPC, market, lot or date coding, net quantity, pack count, complete ingredients and allergens, applicable chocolate-category wording, total delivered cost and storage requirements. A historical claim additionally needs a dated matched predecessor package, receipt or archived primary label and a documented mapping to the current version. Calculate price per common weight and per accepted serving only after resolving product-form and pack ambiguities. Unresolved identity, ingredient, weight, historical or jurisdiction cells remain unknown and block a recipe-change or shrinkflation verdict.
rules.reversible_office_candy_trial_v1: After allergy, dietary, identity and current-label gates pass, purchase only a small reversible quantity. Serve equal coded portions in randomized or counterbalanced order at the same temperature and comparable freshness, record participant eligibility, acceptance, actual consumption, repeat choice and waste using predeclared thresholds, and retain a familiar accepted control. The trial can estimate local office fit under tested conditions; it cannot prove historical recipe continuity, population-wide quality, legal classification in every market, or a universal brand winner.
rules.evidence_bounded_office_candy_stocking_v: The packet does not justify bulk-buying the offer with the largest displayed rating or accepting folklore that a named brand quietly changed. First retain the rating denominator and exact offer ambiguities, verify the current physical label and applicable market, require dated matched evidence for formula or size history, calculate comparable-unit and accepted-serving cost, and run a small matched office trial. Choose only the lowest total-cost exact offer that clears identity, current ingredients, allergen, dietary, budget and trial thresholds. If no offer clears them, use an already accepted control or defer. Do not issue a universal brand-quality, recipe-change, shrinkflation or legal-category verdict.
